newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher in active trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher on Wednesday in active trading, led by a rise in small- and medium- capitalization stocks, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.74 percent, or 1.26 points, to 203.94 on all-share turnover of 102 million shekels against 101 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index gained 0.39 percent to 214.57.

"The positive trend in the market is continuing and activity is strong," said Izik Winish of Capital Securities, but warned: "The market rose sharply during the last few days and we might see some profit-taking in the coming days."
Nevertheless, he said: "The mood in the market is positive and investors are very optimistic."
The main gainers on Wednesday were the small cap stocks traded in the Kerem framework and the smaller stocks traded in the Mishtamim. The blue chip stocks that compose the Maof index were mixed.

"The Maof shares posted only mild rises because of profit- taking. On Tuesday the market rose sharply, but it is still too early to talk about a (longer-term) positive trend in the market," said a trader at Bank Hapoalim.

"We will see a real change in the market only after approval of the 1997 budget and a reduction in the interest rate," the Poalim said. "Nevertheless, the fact that volume remained high today is positive."
Parliament has until December 31 to approve the budget.
The most active shares were Koor Industries, which closed unchanged at 27,948 on volume of 7.5 million shekels, and Bank Hapoalim, which gained 1.0 percent to 498 on turnover of 4.3 million shekels.

Bezeq Israel Telecom, the third most active share, fell 1.0 percent to 815 on volume of 4.2 million shekels. Sahar Securities, an Israeli brokerage, rated the share a buy, despite the fact that its key international-calling business is being opened up to competition.
